articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Wiener, Richardson-Lucy, and Total Variation Techniques for Astronomical Images*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Astronomical images captured by ground-based telescopes are often degraded by atmospheric disturbances, commonly known as the "seeing effect," which causes significant blurring. Addressing this challenge, this study explores the efficacy of three deconvolution techniques—Wiener Deconvolution, Richardson-Lucy Deconvolution (RL), and Total Variation Deconvolution (TV)—on astronomical images. To facilitate a controlled comparison, this research utilized ten high-quality images from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST), which inherently lack atmospheric seeing effects. These images were artificially blurred using an Airy Point Spread Function (PSF) to simulate ground-based observations. The performance of each deconvolution method was rigorously evaluated using two well-established metrics: Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM). The results indicate that Wiener Deconvolution outperforms the other techniques in terms of both SSIM and PSNR, making it a superior choice for correcting blur in astronomical images.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Skin Cancer Detection and Classification using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Skin cancer is a potentially lethal disorder that arises from the uncontrolled proliferation of aberrant cells seen in the skin’s outermost layer. Six out of every seven skin cancer-related deaths are caused by the deadly skin disease melanoma. This kind of cancer has already been identified by the application of machine learning to examine different imaging modalities and protein sequences. Hand-engineered characteristics are typically necessary for machine learning, which can be tedious and time-consuming. The scientific community worldwide has undertaken extensive effort to develop extremely accurate automated systems for skin cancer screening to prevent instances of false negative diagnoses. Furthermore, there is a high likelihood of false negative diagnoses in hospitals where dermatologists must diagnose several cases of skin cancer. More significantly, researchers’ attention has been greatly drawn to the identification of lesions in early diagnosis. By examining deep-learning-based convolutional neural networks (CNNs), artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods have aided in the early detection of skin cancer. For this we analyze the three deep learning models, including VGG16, ResNet50, DenseNet121 to identify and categorize seven distinct forms of skin cancer.Out of three models DenseNet121 has highest testing accuracy of 85%,with training accuracy 99%,0.67 weighted average precision, 0.66 weighted average recall , 0.66 weighted average f1-score.

articleTitle: Integrated Testing Framework for μDMA Peripherals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: This paper presents a thorough examination of micro DMA (μDMA) functionality within an integrated test environment incorporating Advanced Peripheral Bus (APB) Bus Functional Model (BFM) and Random Access Memory (RAM). The study focuses on the utilization of APB BFM to configure μDMA and the subsequent interaction with RAM for data read and write operations. Initially, the configuration of μDMA through APB BFM sets the groundwork for data exchange. Subsequently, RAM serves as the intermediary for data transactions, facilitating efficient data transfer in μDMA. The experimental findings provide valuable insights into the performance and reliability of μDMA within this integrated framework, highlighting its potential applications in communication protocols.

articleTitle: Bipartite Photonic Analysis: Terahertz Stripline Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: An antenna serves to convert radio frequency signals into alternating current and vice versa. In this study, a terahertz-frequency dipole antenna is designed using various substrate materials, including GaAs and FR-4. Performance analysis reveals that the silver dipole antenna with GaAs substrate achieves a gain of 1.464 dB and a directivity of 1.982 dBi, while with FR-4 substrate, it shows a gain of 1.563 dB and a directivity of 1.996 dBi. FR-4, although superior at resonant frequency, exhibits poor efficiency at higher frequencies, making it unsuitable as a substrate material for dipole antennas. Additionally, the antenna’s resonant frequency decreases with increasing substrate dielectric.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Circularly Polarized Miniaturized 2T2R MIMO Proximity Coupled Patch Antenna for 6G Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized miniaturized 2x2 (2T2R) MIMO proximity coupled patch antenna has been designed for 6G communication applications. Here, the Multi Input Multi Output feeding technique is utilized to improve the performance. The proposed antenna uses two layered substrates, such as the patch antenna on the upper layer and the microstrip feedline on the lower layer. The resonating frequency has been chosen as 35 GHz for the 6G application. Rogers RT-Duroid 5880 material with a dielectric permittivity of 2.2 has been chosen for the substrate material with minimal dielectric loss, this substrate is ideally suited for high-frequency and broadband applications. The size of the substrate of the single element proximity coupled patch antenna is 6 x 6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a height of 0.508 mm for lower substrate and 0.371 mm and for 2x2 MIMO proximity coupled patch antenna is 12 x 12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> along with a thickness of 0.508 mm for lower substrate and 0.371mm for upper substrate with same dimensions. The primary radiating patch takes on a rectangular shape, employing the proximity coupled technique. Simulation is conducted utilizing the ANSYS HFSS software, where various parameters including Z-parameter, VSWR, S-parameter, gain, directivity, axial ratio, efficiency, and radiation patterns are analyzed. With a gain exceeding 5 dB, the antenna proves highly beneficial for various communication applications. Also, proximity-coupled patch designs such as single element proximity coupled patch antenna are designed to validate the proposed antenna design. Later on, the design of a 2x2 MIMO antenna was converted to a circularly polarized configuration and miniaturized by introducing a slot for better results and wider applications. The antenna is designed for 6G communication applications.

articleTitle: Grid-integrated Photovoltaic System with Reactive and Active Power Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: The incorporation of sustainable energy sources, such as wind and solar electricity, into the contemporary power grid has presented several new management and stability issues. This paper aims to provide sustainable, efficient, and dependable power generation and distribution while taking into account the erratic and unpredictable nature of renewables. Real power control, often referred to as active power control, is the process of controlling electrical output from clean energy sources to match demand. In order to maximize power extraction from the photovoltaic (PV) array, the Perturb and Observe (P&O), a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) technique is employed to continually track and alter the duty cycle for sending switching pulses to the boost converter. A two-level inverter facilitates the AC-DC conversion with pulse-width modulation (PWM) control. A phase-locked loop (PLL) system is employed as well to synchronize the PV system at particular phase angles and frequencies with the grid. To guarantee the provision of reactive as well as active energy under a variety of operating circumstances, a specialized control circuit is meticulously built. Efficient active power control is essential to maintain grid stability and prevent frequency deviations. Reactive power control is equally crucial, as it manages voltage levels and ensures that the power system remains within permissible voltage limits. Utilizing reactive power control devices, such as capacitors and reactors, and advanced control algorithms, grid operators can maintain the system's voltage profile and minimize losses.

articleTitle: When Artificial Intelligence meets Navarasas - Facial Expression Classification in Kathakali Using DSFD and CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Kathakali, an ancient art form that dates back to the 17th century, is renowned for its intricate hand gestures, dance movements, musical accompaniment, elaborate costumes, and makeup. Mastering such an art form is a challenge even for the most dedicated enthusiasts, given its unconventional methods of expression. However, with current advanced technology, we can use this to aid the learning of unfamiliar subjects by classifying factors to help the new learners. In this paper, we focus on classifying one aspect of the play, which is the expressions on the actor’s face given a picture using computer vision methods. To achieve the final model, we use a combination of Dual Shot Face Detector (DSFD) and Convolution Neural Network (CNN) and finally tuning up the epochs of the training process. With our dataset, the proposed model reached an accuracy of 93% among nine classes. This project hopes to introduce Kathakali to a wider audience and facilitate the learning process of this art form.

articleTitle: A Multistage Cascaded Neural Network Model to Identify the Severity of Epileptic Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures, impacting the quality of life for millions of individuals worldwide. Timely and accurate detection of epileptic seizures is crucial for proper diagnosis and effective treatment. Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals provide vital information about brain activity and serve as a valuable tool for epilepsy detection. The methodology opted for this study was an enhanced multilayer feed forward neural network for automatic detection of epilepsy from EEG signals and hence predicting the severity. The authors build a multistage cascaded neural network model for achieving the same. Initially a Simple Artificial Neural Network (SimpleANN) is designed to classify EEG segments into seizure, healthy and interictal. Later a Multilayer Feed Forward Neural Network (MFFNN) is employed for detecting the severity of epileptic patients and hence can be classified into primary and secondary stages. The experimental results showed that the proposed SimpleANN classifier had provided noticeable results, and outperforms all tested classifiers. The study involves the collection of EEG data from a diverse group of patients, including those with epilepsy and healthy individuals. This automated epilepsy identifying system passes through different stages including decomposition, feature extraction for achieving a better performance model. The proposed system was tested and compared with SVM, KNN, MLP and Decision Tree under different measurement metrics. ANN has managed to give an accuracy of 80 - 90% which is significantly higher as compared to other machine learning models. The proposed work can automatically learn complex patterns from EEG data provides an advantage in identifying subtle seizure related features that may not be evident through manual analysis. Furthermore, the model offers real-time capabilities, making it suitable for continuous monitoring of patients at risk of seizures.

articleTitle: Enhancing LLM Performance on Legal Textual Entailment with Few-Shot CoT-based RAG
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs), leveraging extensive data, have become successful in text generation applications. However, their integration into the legal domain presents distinct challenges, prompting deviations in thought processes and potentially misleading outcomes. Such discrepancies can significantly impact the efficacy of legal text applications. In our study, we propose a novel approach that combines retrieval-based methods with generation-based techniques to provide relevant explanations and labels for the given query for legal textual entailment task, leveraging the concept of Chain of Thought (CoT) for reasoning and few-shot prompting. Later, we enhance LLM outputs through the application of various text generation strategies. Our findings demonstrate an enhancement, with a 5% increase in F1 score and a 3% improvement in accuracy when compared with zero-shot baselines. This highlights the effectiveness of utilizing these strategies in specialized fields such as law, where precision and reliability are of utmost importance.

articleTitle: Design and Investigation of Two Port Circularly Polarized Microstrip Array Antenna with High Gain and Pattern Diversity Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: A two port microstrip array antenna is analyzed and organized in this article. Some of the unique features of designed antenna are: (a) loading of stair slot with unequal arm length on patch provides circular polarization features in between 10.35-10.55 GHz; (b) 1*2 array structure improves the gain level to 12.0 dBi; (c) mirror image of stair slot improves the isolation level to more than 25 dB; and (d) PEC wall in between the antenna port tilts the radiation pattern by ±30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>, which improves the far-field MIMO parameters. The designed radiators impedance matchning can be enhanceed by using a defected ground structure (DGS). At 10.21-10.65 GHz, the radiator that was designed works with the help pf HFSS and CST-MWS. For X-band applications, the antenna designed has a directive radiation pattern and good diversity value.

articleTitle: A nasal-thermistor based study for continuous monitoring of breathing rate and apnea detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: The proposed study discusses a low-cost respiration rate detection system for continuous health monitoring. The significance of this study relies on the fact that the envisaged system can detect high and low ventilation alongside normal breathing conditions. Moreover, the above system can detect apnea as well. This study employs a thermistor attached to commonly available nebulization mask for primary transduction. The temperature difference between inhaled and exhaled air induces resistance changes in the thermistor, which further changes the output voltage across the above sensor in a potential divider network. Various amplification and filtering techniques are employed to extract a respiratory bio-signal of reasonable quality. A quasi-digital signal corresponding to this bio-signal is obtained. Thus, the respiratory rate can be inferred by measuring the time period of the above-mentioned quasi-digital pulse. The accuracy of the proposed system as a respiratory monitor was verified and compared with the help of a reference bio-instrument. Moreover, the study was conducted in a group of fifteen volunteers of various age groups. The maximum error in measuring RR was less than 1 bpm.

articleTitle: Leveraging Light GBM, MLP, and Extra Tree Classifiers for Early Detection and Prediction of Autism Spectrum Disorder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by challenges in social interaction and communication. Symptoms typically manifest in early childhood and persist into adolescence and adulthood. With the increasing utilization of machine learning techniques in medical research, this paper explores the potential of Light GBM, Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and Extra Tree Classifiers for predicting and analyzing ASD across different age groups. The study evaluates these methodologies using publicly available datasets representing ASD screening in children, adolescents, and adults. The first dataset, focused on ASD screening in children, comprises 292 instances with 21 attributes. The second dataset, pertaining to ASD screening in adult subjects, includes 704 instances with 21 attributes. The third dataset, related to ASD screening in adolescent subjects, consists of 104 instances with 21 attributes. After employing Light GBM, MLP, and Extra Tree Classifiers and addressing missing values, the results indicate promising performance across all datasets, providing valuable insights into the predictive capabilities of these methodologies for ASD screening in different age groups.

articleTitle: Context-based Marwari text clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Today's news is not only produced quickly and in large quantities, but it also originates from a variety of internet sources, including news organizations and websites that help people find jobs. It is usual practice to extract information from English text, however, Marwari, a regional language, has not been fully investigated because of the scarcity of resources. Marwari Vector Space Model for (MVSM), Marwari Synset Vector Space Model for (MSVSM), & the Grouped Entity Marwari Document Matrix (GEMDM) were used to process over 1223 Marwari news items using entity extraction and clustering algorithms. To improve accuracy, we used synset-based dimension reduction techniques. MGEDM performed the best across several datasets when the Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering (HAC) and K-means clustering was evaluated using three measures. MGEDM obtained a purity score of 1.8, an entropy score of 1.4, and positive silhouette’s coefficient.

articleTitle: Advancing Early Autism Detection in Children through Machine Learning-Assisted Spectrogram Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: The diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is characterized by ongoing difficulties with verbal and non-verbal communication, repetitive habits, and social interaction. Electroencephalography (EEG) is one of the most popular techniques for investigating neurological disorders such as autism because of its low cost, excellent temporal resolution, and general availability. However, the analysis of EEG recordings typically generates extensive data with dynamic characteristics, traditionally requiring visual inspection by trained clinicians for ASD detection. This approach is labor-intensive, costly, subjective, prone to errors, and lacks consistency. The aim of this research is to create an effective diagnostic method for the identification of ASD using time-frequency spectrogram images obtained from EEG signals. The process involves preprocessing raw EEG signals using filtering, followed by the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) to convert them into spectrogram images. Machine learning (ML) techniques are then used to evaluate these images. The spectrogram images are processed to extract features, which are then inputted into five distinct ML classifiers, including k-Nearest Neighbor (kNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), and Naive Bayes (NB), to perform classification. The system achieved an accuracy of 92.7% when employing kNN. Its simplicity and high performance suggest it could serve as a valuable decision support tool for healthcare practitioners in diagnosing ASD.

articleTitle: A Novel Generator Coupled Dual Battery Energy Management System for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) signify a significant advancement in transportation technology, offering a cleaner and more sustainable alternative to traditional gasoline-powered cars. However, challenges such as battery charging infrastructure, extended charging times, high costs, limited range, and battery degradation remain critical issues in EV evaluation. This paper proposes a novel, compact design for electric vehicles aimed at enhancing sustainable transportation. The design features a gearless wheel system that integrates directly coupled motors with a dual battery energy management system. In this configuration, one battery serves as the primary power source for driving the motors connected directly to the wheels. The second battery is paired with shunt generators, which are also connected to the wheels. The wheel-mounted generators charge one of the batteries while the other battery powers the vehicle, effectively creating a system that reduces the need for external charging. This dual battery setup not only enhances the vehicle's practicality for long-distance travel but also diminishes reliance on traditional charging infrastructure. To validate this design concept, a prototype model was constructed and tested. The prototype demonstrated that the design achieves a compact, charging-free solution, confirming its feasibility for further development and implementation. This approach represents a significant step toward more practical and efficient electric transportation, addressing key challenges in the current EV technology landscape.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Packet Compression Techniques for NoC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Network-on-Chip (NoC) communication plays a vital role in modern multi-core processors. As the number of cores increases, so does the traffic on the NoC, leading to congestion and high latency. Data compression techniques offer a promising approach to reduce network traffic and improve performance. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of various data compression methods suitable for NoC communication, focusing on their impact on network latency. We compare the different performance metrics like compression ratios achieved by different techniques and discuss their trade-offs with respect to complexity and latency overhead.

articleTitle: Real Time Vulnerability Analysis & Risk Prioritization using Zensar’s Risk Assessment Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: The identification of real security threats remains a formidable challenge across diverse organizational landscapes. Traditional approaches, such as Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) conducted at regular intervals, often fall short in addressing emerging security threats, particularly Zero Day vulnerabilities. Moreover, the inherent limitations of the VAPT process can result in scenarios where applications appear vulnerable but are not necessarily exploitable. In response to these challenges, this literature proposes a novel framework dubbed ZenRAF (Zensar's Risk Assessment Framework). ZenRAF is designed to enable real-time identification of risks and facilitate their mitigation. Through the implementation of ZenRAF, authors have successfully analyzed risks and established a prioritization scheme for applying mitigations, focusing particularly on vulnerabilities that are exploitable. This framework offers a proactive security threat management approach, empowering organizations to effectively identify, assess, and mitigate risks promptly. By leveraging ZenRAF, organizations can enhance their security posture and safeguard against the evolving landscape of cyber threats.

articleTitle: Enhanced Mobile Robot Obstacle Avoidance: A Reinforcement Learning Approach with State-Dependent Action Set
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: In this paper, we address the challenge of enabling a mobile robot to navigate through environment such as a a hospital corridor while avoiding collisions with obstacles. The main objective of the agent is to navigate through these corridor without colliding with any of the static or dynamic obstacles in its way. The robot or the agent is equipped with three proximity sensors which determines the proximity of the obstacles in it’s respective direction. The learning is achieved through Q-learning algorithm which is a value based reinforcement learning technique. In order to achieve much lesser computational time and cost we implement state dependant actions such that we can decrement the number of iterations for learning. For testing and visualization Python’s Pygame library is involved. The agent undergoes training with a grid-based environment.

articleTitle: Agile Time Quantum Round Robin Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: In multitasking operating systems, CPU scheduling algorithms are accountable for the queuing of tasks for execution on the CPU. The effectiveness of a CPU scheduling algorithm is measured through CPU utilization, throughput, and process waiting times. One such scheduling algorithm is Round Robin (RR), a preemptive methodology that allocates time in quanta (parts) to execute the processes in a loop. The problems with a static quantum, such as too many context switches and process starvation are addressed by the proposed algorithm named Agile Time Quantum Round Robin (ATQRR). The algorithm dynamically modifies the remaining time based on real-time system factors. To ensure a thorough validation, a comprehensive analysis of the existing literature has been undertaken to compare ATQRR with other similar approaches. This review has focused on many criteria, like average turnaround time, waiting times, throughput, context switch overhead, and the fairness of process scheduling.

articleTitle: Efficient Layouts of Complete t-Partite and Complete Networks into 3-Ary n-Cubes for Optimized Parallel Processing in Multiprocessing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Embedding problems has received a lot of attention in the last decades by various research dealt with many inter-connection networks. Through embedding the existing parallel algorithm of an interconnection network can be used for the embedded network, thus it plays a vital role in manipulating the parallel algorithms of interconnection network in multiprocessing systems. A variation of the k -ary n-cube, notable for its adaptive network structure created to provide efficient parallel processing on multicomputers, is the 3-ary n-cube. In this study, complete t-partite graphs and complete graphs are embedded into 3-ary n-cubes with the least wirelengths.

articleTitle: Challenges in training Deep Q Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Deep Q Network (DQN) is a popular deep reinforcement learning algorithm that has shown remarkable performance in solving complex problems in various domains. However, DQN suffers from many challenges including the choice of appropriate hyperparameters, which is a crucial aspect of training DQN models. Many literatures provide information about the algorithm but not much is available which gives an insight into the hyperparameter tuning. The process of training deep RL algorithms often requires a significant amount of time for experimentation to tune the hyperparameters. Hence, numerical experimentation should be done judiciously. This paper provides insight for choosing DQN hyperparameters to improve its performance and reduce training time. We experimented with different hyperparameters such as network architecture, reward function, target update frequency, and exploration strategies to evaluate their impact on the algorithm’s performance. Our results show that the choice of hyperparameters significantly affects the performance of DQN, and selecting them appropriately can improve the model’s convergence rate and stability. Our approach can help researchers speed up the training process and provide a starting point for selecting hyperparameters while using DQN in real-world applications.

articleTitle: EIROB : An Emotionally Intelligent ROBot for Empathetic Support
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Social assistive robots enhance social interaction and well-being by providing companionship and support. Emotional Intelligence in these robots refers to their ability to identify, understand, and respond to human emotions. This study investigates how well a social robot named ‘EIROB’ can engage elderly persons by using Artificial Emotional Intelligence. EIROB employs a Multimodal Emotion Recognition Algorithm and a Multimodal Emotion Expression System to detect the user’s emotional state and generate appropriate responses through an effective dialogue manager. Interaction with EIROB is facilitated by an Android app, which uses the mobile phone’s inbuilt camera and microphone for facial expression and speech sentiment detection. The captured data is processed in the cloud that enables the model to be deployed remotely. This study aims to create an empathetic interaction model for senior citizens particularly during pandemics like COVID-19 to prevent feelings of isolation. The performance of the emotion recognition models is evaluated via accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score to ensure the effectiveness of the system in recognizing and responding to user’s emotional states.

articleTitle: Addressing Low Frequency Circulating Current Challenges in Solar Grid-Connected Systems with Parallel Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: As the adoption of solar grid-connected systems continues to rise, addressing challenges associated with circulating current becomes increasingly crucial. In such systems employing parallel inverters, low-frequency circulating currents often pose significant issues, impacting system performance and reliability. This paper presents an in-depth analysis of low-frequency circulating currents in solar grid-connected systems with parallel inverters. Comprehensive simulations and analysis is done by varying system parameters like voltage, frequency, phase etc.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection and Classification Using Deep Neural Network and Interpretation Using XAI Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Clinical decision-making relies heavily on accurate brain tumor diagnosis from MRI imaging. Manual interpretation is time-consuming and error-prone. To enhance efficiency, automated techniques using deep neural networks (DNNs), particularly Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs), are proposed. This study incorporates explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) for interpretability. By addressing the need for automated and accurate diagnosis, this research aims to improve patient care and treatment outcomes, providing medical professionals with a dependable tool for brain tumor identification in clinical practice.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Flood Susceptibility Mapping of the Chennai Floods of 2023
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Rapid and precise urban flood forecasting is crucial for promptly implementing preventive actions. This article presents a review of the literature focusing on soft computing techniques and algorithms for predicting urban floods. We also present two famous machine learning algorithms viz., Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost to create a Flood Susceptibility Map (FSM) for the city of Chennai in the state of Tamil Nadu, India based on the historical data of the 2023 floods of Chennai. A decent classification accuracy of 65% and 70% has been achieved using our approach for both RF and XGBoost algorithms respectively.

articleTitle: Credit Endorsement Forecast Utilizing Troupe Learning and XGBoost
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: The current approaches to predicting loan approval frequently depend on oversimplified models that are unable to account for the complexity of borrower behaviour and financial risk assessment. One disadvantage is that the model's capacity to identify various patterns and subtleties in the data is restricted by its dependence on a single machine learning technique. This research proposes a framework for predicting loan acceptance that optimizes bank resources by reducing the risk involved in choosing safe candidates for loans through the use of ensemble learning techniques, specifically XGBoost. We make use of a Kaggle dataset with 4269 observations and 13 characteristics, including financial and demographic data. We obtain promising accuracies of 98% and 95%, respectively, by utilizing XGBoost and ensemble learning techniques as Random Forest, SVC, KNN, and Logistic Regression. Our research highlights how machine learning may improve the loan approval process, which can lead to better resource allocation and decision-making in banking operations.

articleTitle: Economic Design of Variables Modified Double Sampling Plan under Double Specification Limits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: In this article, we investigate an economic design of a variable modified double sampling plan to select the optimal parameters that minimize the total quality cost of the manufactured products. The suggested sampling plan can be applied for the inspection of the quality characteristics which are measured on a numerical scale with double specification limits. The economic plan parameters of the proposed sampling plan are determined by formulating an optimization model. The optimization problem is formulated as a nonlinear programming problem where the minimization of total cost is used as an objective function and the constraints are related to probabilities of acceptance of the lot at acceptable quality level and limiting quality level under the operating characteristic curve. A comparative study is also provided to show the effectiveness of the suggested plan. A real time application is also provided to explain the implementation of the suggested economic modified double sampling plan.

articleTitle: Forensic Automatic Speaker Recognition: Coping with Impersonated Speech
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Forensic Automatic Speaker Recognition (FASR) systems are essential for authenticating individuals based on speech characteristics in forensic contexts. The efficacy of the system is investigated through an experiment featuring five celebrities to evaluate the accuracy of identifying whether a test speech belongs to a genuine speaker or an impersonator. A database consisting of recordings from a selected number of celebrities and impersonated speech recordings from professional mimicry artists (who are good at mimicking these celebrities) are used for the experiment described in this paper. Mel-spectrograms of both original and impersonated speech are used to train a CNN model, and the performance of the model is evaluated using performance metrics such as accuracy, recall, and precision. The system gives an overall accuracy of 84.93% while evaluating the CNN models corresponding to 5 different celebrities.

articleTitle: EmoClass: Subject-Independent Emotion Classification for BCI Systems Using EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) explores the interaction between humans and technology, considering emotional responses as an integral part of human life. Emotions are significant influencers of decision-making, and public well-being, intricately linked to mental health, detectable through BrainComputer Interface (BCI) technologies. BCI provides insights into neural correlates of emotional states and aids in mental health assessment and intervention strategies. Electroencephalography (EEG) based BCI systems play a significant role in classifying emotions to enhance human interaction. The proposed models were applied to a PhyMER dataset for emotion classification, encompassing both binary and multi-class models using a subject-independent approach. The features are extracted from EEG signals using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and Peak-to-Peak (P2P) analysis. The proposed binary and multiclass models were analyzed to classify the emotions using a variety of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) algorithms. The performance metrics of the binary and multiclass ML models have maximum F1 scores of 62.04 and 28.48 respectively. Additionally, the binary and multiclass DL model achieved a maximum F1 score of 61.31 and 29.2 respectively.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of Poultry Diseases using Implicit Pattern Mining over Explicit Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Early detection of poultry diseases is crucial for poultry farmers, but traditional identification methods are often slow and tedious due to limited facilities. We present a comprehensive evaluation of implicit pattern mining techniques using lightweight, CNN-based deep learning models such as, MobileNetV2, InceptionV3, and EfficientNetB5 that are amenable for implementation on edge devices. We contrast them with traditional machine learning approaches applied to analyse chicken fecal image data to classify images of healthy samples from unhealthy ones. We use model interpretation to gain insight to the patterns in the input image that the deep learning models use to make predictions. This facilitates corroborating domain understanding with model performance. This study demonstrates the viability of deploying deep learning based methods for poultry disease detection on handheld devices, highlighting its potential for deployment in the field.

articleTitle: Progressively Stacked Serial Encoder Decoder For MRI Super Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Low-resolution MRI images in the through-plane direction impose constraints on both time and cost. This insufficient level of resolution does not meet the requirements for high-resolution imaging that is necessary for early diagnosis of brain diseases and morphometric analysis. Conventional single-image super-resolution (SISR) techniques have significant obstacles, such as effectively integrating intricate local details with the overall anatomical structure. In order to address these difficulties, we propose a novel technique known as the Progressively Serial-Stacked Encoder Decoder (PSSED) to improve the resolution of brain MRI scans. This approach employs convolutional blocks to extract specific information and enhance the quality of the image. Our strategy has been proven to be superior to previous Single Image Super-Resolution (SISR) methods based on extensive experimentation using publically available datasets. Our findings highlight the potential of deep learning techniques to address the constraints of low-resolution MRI images, paving the path for improved diagnostic accuracy and lower radiation exposure in clinical practice.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Health Monitoring System for High-Risk Cardiac Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: In biomedical applications, monitoring cardiac patients is a challenging task. Thus, the goal of our research is to design and construct a portable, lightweight, affordable telecardiac device that will allow remote cardiac patient monitoring. An arrhythmia detector based on temperature changes is being built with the help of MATLAB tools. In this case, advanced wavelet decomposition methods are being used. As technology develops, more people are paying attention to their health. The heart is the most vital organ in the body. In this paper, the QRS complex detector uses 108 sets from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database and achieved Sensitivity of 97.62% with SNR of 19.76 dB.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Fire Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Fires pose unpredictable threats to life, property, and the environment, making timely detection imperative for initiating rapid response measures and mitigating potential disasters. Recognizing this critical need, our project introduces a state-of-the-art Deep Learning-Based Fire Detection System. This system integrates both fire and smoke detection, addressing a gap often overlooked in conventional methods where smoke, a primary indicator of early fire stages, significantly enhances the system’s responsiveness to potential dangers. Our system, leveraging the advanced YOLO v8 architecture, is tailored to operate effectively in outdoor environments where fires can be equally destructive but are typically more challenging to detect. The proposed system demonstrates exceptional performance, achieving a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.918 and a recall rate of 0.99, underscoring its efficacy and reliability. By addressing the pressing need for early detection and highlighting the critical role of smoke detection, our innovative approach significantly enhances safety measures. Additionally, the system’s adaptability to diverse outdoor conditions and its integrated alert system make it a crucial tool in advancing fire detection and prevention efforts, thereby safeguarding lives, property, and the environment.

articleTitle: Efficient Optimization of Dual Port Circularly Polarized 1*2 Array based Microstrip Antenna using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: This work studies the design and optimisation of a two-port high gain printed antenna using machine learning algorithms. The following are a few crucial characteristics of the suggested radiating structure: (i) In order to shorten the simulation time, machine learning (ML) techniques based on ANN and random forests are used to predict the reflection coefficient (RC) (|S11|) features of the designed radiator; (ii) Circularly polarized waves in the 10.38-10.45 GHz range are produced by using a stair slot; (iii) A 1*2 array structure yields high gain, or 7.5 dBi, within the operating frequency range; and (iv) polarization diversity concept is provided by opposite orientation of aperture, which raises the isolation level to more than 30 dB. It is established that the intended radiator functions between 10.37-10.55 GHz by comparing the findings of the HFSS and CST with the predictions made by the ML algorithm. The suitability of the suggested radiator for X-band applications is approved by good values for the diversity and far-field characteristics.

articleTitle: A Wideband Miniaturized Microstrip Antenna for Sub-8 GHz New Radio for 6G Connectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: A miniaturized microstrip antenna with loaded circular slots on a rectangular patch for application in the new radio band for future sixth generation ubiquitous seamless connectivity is presented. The proposed design has a good impedance matched VSWR bandwidth. Good return loss and good radiating pattern characteristic are observed at desired new radio band. The antenna is designed as a miniaturized plane geometry with line fed symmetric circular slots. Miniaturization was achieved after considering several techniques like loading and reshaping of antenna, shorting and folding. The antenna is etched on flexible RT Duroid substrate. Simulation was done using CST Microwave Studio. The parametrics affecting the quality factor and return losses of the antenna like ground plane dimension, substrate and patch dimensions are analyzed.

articleTitle: Identification of Paddy Leaf Disease using Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: The skill of growing fruits and vegetables is known as horticulture, and it is the foundation of both business and well-being. Crop observation and disease detection have even taken precedence over conventional methods of modern farming, despite those techniques being rendered outdated by ignorance of plant illnesses, which can result in financial losses. Plant disease detection and treatment strategies are becoming more sophisticated as horticulture moves toward the Industrial Internet of things (IIoT) 5.0. This effort focuses on creating a model that can precisely diagnose rice leaf disease by examining the leaves of rice plants in order to accomplish this aim. Utilizing a logistic regression classification algorithm, the ResNet50 model based on R-CNN has been evaluated with a dataset of plant leaf image information. 97% accuracy is attained with the Resnet-50 model when compared with other models namely, DenseNet-161 and Inception Net V3 +RCNN.

Author Keywords: Plant leaf disease diagnosis deep learning

articleTitle: AI-based Diabetic Retinopathy Grading Using Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is a progressive eye condition caused by prolonged high blood sugar levels in individuals with diabetes, leading to damage in the blood vessels of the retina. It can result in vision impairment or blindness if left untreated, making early detection and management crucial for preserving eyesight. Employing neural networks for image classification can help overcome these challenges. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can automatically extract relevant features and classify images into different categories, aiding in early diagnosis and intervention. It also offers a promising avenue for improving DR screening, particularly in areas with limited access to ophthalmologists. This paper aims to enhance DR grading performance by implementing a hardware solution using Raspberry Pi. One significant advantage of this approach is the potential for costeffective and portable screening in resource-limited settings. By leveraging the Raspberry Pi’s affordability and compact form factor, healthcare providers can deploy screening systems in remote areas where access to traditional medical infrastructure is limited

articleTitle: Planar Complementary Spiral Sensor for Permittivity Characterization of Oil Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: A planar complementary spiral sensor (PCSS) for the characterization of the permittivity (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) of oil samples is proposed in this paper. A monopole antenna coupled with a complementary spiral resonator is utilized to test the oil samples. The resonant frequency of the proposed sensor is 2.4 GHz in ISM frequency band. The sensor is fabricated on FR4 substrate with dielectric constant (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>) of 4.4, loss tangent (tanδ) of 0.02 and thickness (h) of 1.6mm. The overall dimensions of the PCSS are 13 mm x 10 mm x 1.6 mm. An empirical formula is derived for the extraction of the ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> of oil samples. Additionally, the paper presents a method for adulteration detection of coconut oil. High sensitivity and compact size are highlighted as the key features of PCSS.

articleTitle: Direction Finding in Time Modulated Linear Arrays Using Supervised Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: In Time Modulated Arrays (TMAs), the spectrum characteristics of the time modulated signal vary with each incident angle. In this paper, a novel idea of the feasibility of Machine Learning (ML) approach for the Direction of Arrival (DoA) estimation in a two-element Time Modulated Linear Array (TMLA) is proposed. The Fourier components of the received TMLA signal are used as the input data for training. The DoA estimation of signal from a single source is formulated as a multiclassification problem with single label. The performance of the classification based method is tested under various SNR conditions. The regression based method for estimating off-grid angles is also studied.

articleTitle: Quantum Anti-Spyware Protocols for Fault Injection Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Multi-tenancy schemes for quantum computing hardware are vulnerable to fault injection attacks through crosstalk effects. Research studies have experimentally demonstrated the change in output probabilities of victim circuits where the victim and the adversary share the same quantum hardware. To detect adversary circuits, this paper proposes compile time and simulation based protocols to scan quantum computer programs for malicious code patterns. In the compile time approach, with the help of databases of known malicious patterns, the number of gates and the repeating patterns in the code structures are tracked and validated for malicious intent. In the simulation based approach, Idle Tomography (IDT) using pyGSTi software framework is employed for crosstalk error rate extraction. Hamiltonian and Stochastic errors of relevant qubit pairs in accordance with the quantum hardware’s connectivity mapping are analyzed for the detection of unrecognized malicious adversary patterns. Both the protocols output metrics and error rates information that can be used as a "confidence ruler" over a concerned quantum hardware. These protocols safeguard honest quantum circuit parties from possible interference and resulting tampered computational outcomes brought about by adversary parties.

articleTitle: StressDetect: A Deep Learning Approach for Mental Stress Detection Using Time-Frequency Representation of EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Mental stress is a prominent issue affecting individuals worldwide, necessitating efficient detection methods for timely intervention and support. Electroencephalography (EEG)based stress detection has emerged as a promising approach due to its non-invasive nature and high temporal resolution. In this paper, we present "StressDetect," a novel deep learning model designed for mental stress detection using EEG signals. Our approach involves generating time-frequency representations of EEG signals through the utilization of complex Morlet wavelets and Fourier coefficients. Subsequently, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture is designed and trained on the obtained time-frequency plots, using a series of convolution and pooling layers for feature extraction. A softmax layer is employed for binary classification, distinguishing between stress and non-stress states. The proposed TF-CNN model is evaluated through a series of experiments conducted on subsets of mental tasks, yielding promising results with a maximum accuracy of 97.61% in stress detection. The experimental results showcase the robustness, generalizability and efficiency of the model by outperforming the existing techniques.

articleTitle: Secure Ration Provision: Ethereum Blockchain Powered Supply Chain Management for India's Public Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Exploring the Application of Blockchain Technology in India's Public Distribution System (PDS), this paper addresses inefficiencies within the supply chain and enhances its transparency. The focus is on developing a Decentralized Application (dApp) for the PDS, with the primary aim to improve transparency and efficiency and ensure food security among millions of vulnerable individuals. The proposed system provides a transparent and immutable record of transactions throughout the supply chain, enhancing overall efficiency and effectiveness while addressing issues of accountability and data integrity. The methodology involves developing a comprehensive system architecture for integrating blockchain into the existing PDS infrastructure and creating a permissioned blockchain network to ensure only authorized participants engage. This has implications not only for PDS management but also for similar systems globally.

articleTitle: A Study of Digital Modulation Schemes over Multi-Cluster Fluctuating Two-Ray Fading Channels for Terahertz Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) based communication is currently being explored as a potential solution for achieving high data rate transmission in wireless communication. Understanding the impact of fading channels on THz communication is important because it can help in the design and optimization of THz communication systems. A new family of fading channels called Multi-cluster Fluctuating Two-Ray (MFTR) channel model can be utilized for THz transmission. This fading model is made up of two fluctuating specular components with unpredictable phases and a clustering of scattered waves. The digital modulation schemes are essential for communication channels due to their ability to provide robustness against the effects of fading and high spectral efficiency. In this paper, the performance analysis of modulation schemes and the outage probability over MFTR fading channels are evaluated. The performance metrics are derived using the probability-based approach. A comparison of coherent modulation and the non-coherent modulation over this fading channel are also presented. The derived resulted expressions are plotted and analysed along with the impacts fading parameters over performance of MFTR fading channels. For validation, Monte-Carlo simulation is used.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Enabled Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the impact of integrating reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) in cognitive radio (CR) networks for the enhancement of spectrum sensing and data transmission for unlicensed users (ULU) in a limited energy environment. The idea is to use RIS to help ULU in spectrum sensing as well as energy harvesting operations so that the CR networks perform more efficiently and have better spectral efficiency. To get the full potential of RIS, we employed a nature-inspired soft computing technique named Grey-Wolf optimization (GWO) to tune the reflecting phase of the RIS as needed. With the support of RIS, we investigate the usage of non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) technique for data transmission across multiple users. We illustrate the effectiveness of this integrated approach through simulation and provide the receiver operating characteristics (ROC) curve for spectrum sensing performance and outage probability for spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: Field Size-based Packet Header Anomaly Detection with Rule-Based Normal Profile Updating for Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Packet Header Anomaly Detection, or PHAD, is a technique for detecting network intrusion. It assigns scores to a packet using some method and uses these scores to predict whether this packet is benign or anomalous. In this method, the genuine packets usually seen in a network are used to create the profile of header fields. During testing, packet header fields are extracted and compared with the values in this profile. A score is assigned to each packet based on the presence or absence of each header field of the packet in the profile. This score is compared with a threshold, and a label is assigned to the packet. Researchers employ two methods for generating the score: stationary and non-stationary methods. The main issue with this PHAD technique is the large amount of false alarms generated. To reduce these false alarms without compromising other parameters, a modified PHAD scheme with a new scoring method and the introduction of a mechanism to update the profile during the testing phase is proposed in this work. The proposed method was tested on two publicly available datasets, and the results show that the technique can reduce false alarms by about 11% without causing any reduction in the other parameters.

articleTitle: Harnessing Image Analysis for Early Leukemia Detection in Bone Marrow Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: White blood cells, or leukocytes, are important in determining a person's health since they can alter the immune system, leading to infections, anemia, leukemia, and other issues. Blood cancer is caused by these white blood cells proliferating beyond control. In this article, we develop a model for identifying and classifying cancer white blood cells using convolutional neural networks (CNNs). We train and test with the Bone Marrow Microscopic Images of Blood Samples dataset. CNN initially processes the submitted photographs. The max pooling and convolution layers then collect features, with the convolution layer handling classification and the fully connected layer handling feature extraction. The contour technique is utilized when the output indicates that the cells are cancerous. The contour approach aids in the segmentation process by allowing for the localization of the afflicted cell. The photographs in the collection are organized into four categories: neutrophils, eosinophils, monocytes, and lymphocytes. The output image shows the type of damage, as well as the mapping of the afflicted cell.

articleTitle: CNN Based Plant Leaf Disease Detection Using Raw Leaf Images for Efficient Plant Health Monitoring in Agricultural IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Agriculture is a major economic driver of both the high and low income countries across the globe. Hence it is important to modernize agricultural practices by incorporating modern technological developments as a continuous process. Among the various challenges, plant leaf diseases pose a significant threat, leading to reduced agricultural yields and economic losses. Early detection of these diseases is crucial for timely intervention, yet traditional methods relying on human visual inspection are often delayed, incomplete, and unreliable. To address this, our study employs a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to analyze plant leaf images taken from New plant dataset, resulting in a highly accurate model for detecting various leaf diseases of Apple, Potato, Strawberry and Tomato. The developed CNN model achieved an accuracy of 90.91%, offering a promising tool for improving agricultural productivity by minimizing disease-induced crop damage.

articleTitle: A Non-isolated Bidirectional Buck-Boost DC-DC Converter with Minimum Component Count
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel non-isolated high gain DC-DC converter designed to perform bidirectional buck boost operations in both the power flow directions efficiently. The converter is engineered with an emphasis on simplicity, utilizing a minimal number of components. Its standout feature lies in its broad duty ratio range, enhancing adaptability to meet the specific demands of renewable energy sources and electric vehicle applications. Noteworthy for its straightforward control and design characteristics, the proposed topology employs small signal analysis and the K-factor method for controller design. To rigorously validate the performance, open-loop and closed loop simulations of the proposed converter are conducted using MATLAB Simulink, considering a power level of 300 watts. This comprehensive examination ensures a thorough understanding of the converter's behavior and effectiveness in various operational scenarios.

Author Keywords: Applications in Electric Vehicles and Renewable Energy System

articleTitle: Intelligent Water Quality Assessment System For Industrial Regions : Integrating Sensors, IoT and Random Forest Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: This paper focuses on the development of an intelligent water quality assessment system that integrates sensors, Internet of Things (IoT) technology, and random forest classification. Water quality assessment plays a crucial role in safeguarding public health and environmental sustainability. Traditional methods often suffer from limitations such as time-consuming manual sampling and analysis processes. In response, this project proposes a novel approach leveraging colorimetric paper sensors and IoT connectivity to assess water quality. The collected data are then processed using the random forest classification algorithm to classify water quality levels and identify potability of the water sample. The integration of these technologies enables proactive and automated monitoring, facilitating timely interventions and decision-making for water management authorities. Through the implementation of this intelligent system, it is anticipated that water quality monitoring processes will become more efficient, accurate, and cost-effective, ultimately contributing to the protection of human health and the environment.

articleTitle: A Novel Circular Flux Dual Rotor Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Dual rotor generators are pivotal devices for power generation, and certain design modifications can continuously enhance power output without changing the fundamental design structure. Modern energy production heavily relies on dual rotor generators, which utilize a stator and rotor rotating mechanism. Existing dual rotor generators typically operate on an axial flux flow mechanism, which has several drawbacks, including the need for a stator auxiliary supply, sensor requirements, complex design, and high maintenance. To address these issues, the authors propose a novel circular flux flow-based dual rotor generator. This new design aims to eliminate the disadvantages of the axial flux flow mechanism. By modifying the physical rotation of the stator winding mechanism along with the rotor rotation, the design enhances flux linkages at various operational speeds, resulting in increased power generation. This paper presents a prototype design of the proposed dual rotor generator. The prototype was tested and achieved maximum power generation at various stator and rotor speed variations. Additionally, the effects of power generation were examined for both clockwise and anticlockwise directions.

articleTitle: Modelling and Stability Analysis of Dynamic Droop Controlled Microgrid based on Dynamic phasor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: The most widely adapted technique for managing the parallel-operated inverters in microgrid applications is droop control. It is a plug-and-play control that doesn't need any kind of communication equipment. Nevertheless, in its traditional form, the droop controller's transient performance is subpar. Therefore, to offset this disadvantage, dynamic droop gains are included in addition to conventional droop. It will enhance system stability and function as a proportional derivative controller. This work develops a stability analysis and dynamic phasor-based modelling for a dynamic droop controlled microgrid system. By setting an appropriate control objective, particle swarm optimization is used to optimize the controller parameters. The characteristic equation is developed for both dynamic and conventional microgrid systems with droop control. The corresponding impulse response is plotted which will allows for the performance evaluation of the dynamic droop regulated microgrid systems. The improvement in stability depending on the eigenvalue location is demonstrated by the simulation results. Furthermore, there is a noticeable enhancement in both peak overshot and settling time performance.

articleTitle: Optimizing Loss Functions in Conditional GANs for Astronomical Image Deconvolution: A Comparative Study at Varied Epochs*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: This study explores the optimization of loss functions in conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (cGANs), specifically the pix2pix model, for the deconvolution of astronomical images obtained from the Hubble Space Telescope. The objective is to mitigate the effects of atmospheric distortion, commonly referred to as the "seeing" effect. We systematically evaluated various combinations of Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) with logits as loss functions for the generator. These were tested at different training epochs—10, 20, 30, 40, and 50. Our results indicate that a specific weighting of BCE with logits, MAE, and SSIM—1, 1, and 50, respectively—significantly enhances the performance, yielding higher Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and SSIM values post 30 epochs. In addition, we compared our cGAN-based method with conventional techniques, including Wiener deconvolution, Richardson-Lucy algorithm, and Total Variation (TV) deconvolution. Our proposed method demonstrated superior clarity and detail retention.

articleTitle: Legal Assistance Redefined: Transforming Legal Access with AI-Powered LegalLink
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: In today’s scenario, securing prompt and accurate legal aid remains tough for many due to India’s complex legal system, a scarcity of lawyers, high fees, and widespread legal unawareness. To address these issues, we plan to create a comprehensive chatbot designed to provide easy access to valuable legal information for the general public. The LegalLink chatbot leverages the Nomic AI text encoder for encoding user queries, followed by the Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) model for retrieving and integrating external knowledge sources into prompt templates. Additionally, it utilizes the Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 model for generating contextually rich and accurate responses tailored to legal inquiries. This paper outlines the chatbot’s architecture, various ML models used, and the methodology adopted. Leveraging cutting-edge artificial intelligence, LegalLink revolutionizes the way people access legal guidance, offering timely, accurate, and user-friendly assistance.

articleTitle: A Low Complexity Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Model of Chikmagalur, Karnataka, India
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: In order to create a landslip susceptibility map (LSM) for the district of Chikmagalur in the state of Karnataka, South India, this article offers an artificial neural network (ANN) model. The following landslide conditioning factors (LCF) were taken into account during the development, testing, validation, and training of the LSM: elevation, slope, aspect, curvature, stream power index (SPI), rainfall, normalized differential vegetation index (NDVI), lithology and land use and cover. Following creation, the LSM is tested using landslide and non-landslide sites and the ANN model that is suggested produces an accuracy of 86%.

articleTitle: Generation of Bloom’s taxonomy-based complex-level questions using knowledge graph
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: In the landscape of educational technology, the present scenario in question generation often involves static and predefined assessments that may not adequately gauge students’ diverse cognitive abilities. The relevance of a knowledge graph in this context lies in its ability to capture the inherent connections and hierarchies within a domain, fostering a more intelligent and context-aware question generation process. This research proposes a novel approach to question generation, leveraging the knowledge graph. The knowledge graph serves as a dynamic representation of interconnected concepts, offering a structured framework for understanding relationships between topics. This, in turn, enables a more nuanced and contextually relevant selection of keywords for question formulation. Unlike traditional question generation methods, this model harnesses the power of semantic relationships encoded in the knowledge graph to align questions with Bloom’s Taxonomy levels, ensuring a spectrum of complexity. This innovative approach not only modernizes question generation but also aligns assessments more closely with real-world problem-solving scenarios, ultimately contributing to a more effective and personalized learning experience.

articleTitle: Spectral Efficiency Analysis for mmWave Full Duplex Multihop IAB Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: The availability of wider bandwidth in mmWave frequencies has made it an attractive option for future wireless communication. 3GPP Release 16 introduced Integrated Access and Backhaul (IAB), a cost-efficient solution for small cell deployments. Hybrid analog/digital beamforming is a promising approach to mitigate high path loss and enhance beamforming gain, as fully digital beamforming is impractical and fully analog beamforming has limitations in multiuser scenarios. We examined a multihop IAB network with nodes operating in full-duplex mode. Data transmissions occur on the backhaul uplink from the gNodeB (gNB) to the first IAB node and on the access downlink from the first IAB node to the first user. This process repeats from the first IAB node to the second IAB node and from the second IAB node to the second user. To reduce self-interference (SI) and improve spectral efficiency, we propose hybrid precoders and combiners. Simulations demonstrate that our hybrid beamforming method significantly outperforms existing models and approaches the upper bound of fully digital beamforming.

articleTitle: Quantum Enhanced Prediction for Breast Cancer Electronic Health Records
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Quantum computing technology allows for more efficient problem-solving and provides essentially distinct answers to computational challenges when compared to classical computations. Machine learning algorithms have come to the fore in medical research and offer promising avenues for increasing the accuracy of cancer diagnosis. Breast cancer represents the majority of cancer cases in women worldwide, making it a serious and widespread public health issue. Improving patient outcomes requires early identification of cancer. The proposed Quantum Enhanced Prediction (QEP) project delves into the predictive power of two distinct learning paradigms: Support Vector Machine and Quantum Support Vector Machine, using Wisconsin breast cancer dataset. The research underscores the complexity of algorithms in cancer prediction. A departure from the ZZ feature map in QSVM marked the beginning of an intentional shift from traditional design. However, the study looked at the integration of the Z element map and Pauli matrices, providing the foundation for improved accuracy and a better grasp of quantum mechanics in cancer prediction. This conceptual shift intends to investigate the possible influence of quantum computing on breast cancer prediction with more granularity.

articleTitle: Optimizing Recommendation Systems: Analyzing the Impact of Imputation Techniques on Individual and Group Recommendation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: In today’s world, Recommendation Systems play a significant role in guiding and simplifying the decision-making process for individuals and groups. However, the presence of missing data in user-item interaction matrices poses a challenge to accurately identify user preferences and provide relevant suggestions. This is particularly true for group recommendation systems that cater to multiple users. To address this challenge, we have applied four imputation techniques to individual and group recommendation models, including User-based Collaborative filtering, Matrix factorization using Singular Value Decomposition, and deep learning-based models like Autoencoders. We evaluated the effectiveness of these techniques using root mean squared error and mean absolute error metrics and observed a significant impact on the quality of recommendations. Additionally, we implemented aggregation strategies like Borda count, Additive Utilitarian, Multiplicative Utilitarian, Least Misery, and Most Pleasure for Group Recommendations. We evaluated the performance of these strategies using satisfaction score and disagreement score. Overall, our findings suggest that imputation techniques can significantly improve the quality of recommendations in both individual and group recommendation systems.

articleTitle: Harnessing Generative AI for IoT Enhanced Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques with the Internet of Things (IoT) to revolutionize educational paradigms. Leveraging Generative AI, such as deep learning models, alongside IoT devices opens up new avenues for personalized and immersive learning experiences. Through the analysis of real-time data collected by IoT sensors, coupled with Generative AI's ability to synthesize content, educational environments can be dynamically adapted to individual learning styles and preferences. This abstract presents a framework for the synergy between Generative AI and IoT, emphasizing their combined potential to create interactive educational platforms. By harnessing Generative AI for content generation and IoT for data collection and analysis, educational systems can be tailored to cater to diverse learners, fostering engagement, retention, and comprehension. The integration of these technologies promises to reshape the landscape of education, offering adaptive, interactive, and enriched learning experiences for students across various disciplines and demographics.

articleTitle: Analysis on the consensus algorithms with reputation-based incentives in the healthcare blockchain networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Signal Processing, Informatics, Communication and Energy Systems (SPICES)
abstract: Blockchain technology has gained significant attention in the healthcare sector due to its potential to address challenges related to data security, integrity, and interoperability. One critical aspect of blockchain networks is the consensus mechanism, which ensures agreement among distributed nodes on the validity and ordering of transactions. In healthcare blockchain networks, achieving consensus is particularly challenging due to the sensitive nature of healthcare data and the diverse interests of stakeholders. Traditional consensus mechanisms may not suffice to incentivize participation and ensure trust in such environments. This paper presents an analysis of reputation-based incentives as a mechanism to facilitate consensus in healthcare blockchain networks. Reputation systems assign scores or ratings to network participants based on their past behaviour, contributions, and reliability. By incorporating reputation-based incentives into the consensus process, healthcare blockchain networks can incentivize honest behaviour, discourage malicious actors, and improve the overall reliability and trustworthiness of the network.

articleTitle: Advancements in VLSI implementation of lossless ECG signal compression schemes
